idiom_name: Catch2/GoogleTest + committed reference files under testdata/
implementation_notes: The standard library supplies only the plumbing: render the subject's observable output into a canonical string (an explicit operator<< or serializer), read the committed reference with std::ifstream/std::filesystem, compare, and add a --update path that rewrites the reference for review. Nothing provides the record/compare/approve workflow itself, so the harness is hand-written - which stays justified when the artefact is large text a human must approve through a diff tool, or when you do not want a test-only dependency. Use locale-independent formatting (std::to_chars, explicit precision) and fix the newline policy so Windows and POSIX runs agree.
pitfalls: std::filesystem calls throw std::filesystem::filesystem_error on missing or unreadable paths, turning a missing reference into a test error rather than a clean failure; check with exists() or use an error_code overload.
operator<< output is not stable across standard-library versions and locales (floats, container formatting); format explicitly and imbue a fixed locale.
C++17 filesystem may need -lstdc++fs (GCC before 9.1) or -lc++fs (LLVM before 9) at link time, so the harness can fail to build on older toolchains for a reason that has nothing to do with the test.
Dumping raw objects (memcpy/padding) captures indeterminate bytes; only serialize named, canonical fields.

variants.name: ApprovalTests.cpp single-header approval testing
variants.implementation_notes: ApprovalTests.cpp supplies the loop off the shelf: Approvals::verify(value) writes the received output, compares it with the approved file (reporting a diff through the configured reporter/launcher) and leaves acceptance to an explicit human step; the project describes itself as 'also known as Golden Master Tests or Snapshot Testing' and integrates with GoogleTest, Catch2, doctest, CppUTest and Boost.Test. Prefer it where the harness would otherwise be rewritten per project or where the team already accepts a test-only dependency; keep it behind a test target so production builds stay clean.
pitfalls: The received file content is written next to the source by default; CI must be configured to fail rather than accept, and .received.*/approval artefacts should be excluded from commits.
Relying on a GUI diff launcher makes local approval convenient but opaque in headless environments; configure a console reporter for CI and keep the launcher local.
